text:
oliver: Heads up — I chased a reproducible drift and memory growth pattern during long-context runs with paged KV on MI250X (ROCm). After ~30k tokens the model starts hallucinating and tracked VRAM mapping shows page aliasing after cross-GPU migration.

anya: ugh. can you paste repro steps? sequence length, batch, model?

oliver: repro command I used:```bash
./runtest --model small-llama --seq 16384 --batch 1 --mode paged --trace-kv pager.trace
```
short run: cold start ok, then continuous streaming generation with mixed seqs. mem growth ~+600MB over 10k tokens and outputs slowly drift.

mira: did you see any PT owner flips or duplicate physical addr mappings in the trace? sounds like stale owner pointer or missing invalidation.

oliver: yes — pager.trace shows two PT entries mapping same phys page to different virtual slots after eviction+reclaim. snippet from trace:```
# pager.trace excerpt
pt[0x1f3] -> phys 0x7a120 (owner gpu0)
pt[0x1f3] -> phys 0x4b8f0 (owner gpu1)  # after migrate
# no fence seen between remap ops
```

jason: could be missing DMA sync / not waiting for GPU ops to complete before reusing page table entry. On NV we needed an explicit invalidate/fence in our page walker. ROCm page table semantics differ.

anya: did you try forcing local pinning (no migration) as a mitigation?

oliver: pinned pages avoids the aliasing, memory growth stops, perf drops ~8% but stable. quick fix:```json
{"kv":{"pin_policy":"no_migrate"}}
```

mira: interesting. also saw in the profiling that the copy path sometimes races with eviction thread — when a chunk is being copied out over PCIe while the pager reassigns the same PFN to a new allocation it ends up double-referenced in the PT. Could be a hole in our refcounting during async copy completion.

oliver: attaching micro-profile: tokens/sec timeline and mem:```
T=0..10k tokens: 450 t/s, rss stable 12.2GB
T=10k..30k: 430 -> 380 t/s, rss climbs to 12.8GB
After aliasing event: output quality drops, repeated n-grams increase
```

jason: can we get a small reproducer that exercises just the page migrate code path? maybe a tiny loop that force-evicts, migrates, and writes new headers to PT without the model to speed debugging.

oliver: I'll produce a minimal harness today and push to //eng-runtime/kv-repro with trace and nvprof-like ROCm counters. Expect a PR with repro + traces.

infra-bot: new build queued: redwood/kv-pager-debug:b190 -> staging (build 190).

mira: parallel idea: add an extra generation-time assert in dev builds to check for duplicate physical mappings: scan PT for duplicate phys -> if found log full PT dump and refuse to reuse the slot. That should make root cause repros deterministic.

anya: sounds good. also file a ticket linking the traces and include which hw (MI250X driver version, PCIe topology) — those details matter.

oliver: noted: MI250X (ROCm 5.7), PCIe x16 links across CPU root complex, NVLink not present on this node. I filed BUG-3281 and uploaded traces.

jason: FYI, on NVIDIA we had a subtle bug where fallback eviction path used a stale index from the free-list causing a one-off wrap that created PT holes. Might be a different manifestation but worth checking the free-list code path.

oliver: good call. I'll diff free-list code between AMD/NV paths. If anyone wants the immediate workaround: set pin_policy=no_migrate on dedicated workloads handling very long contexts.

deploy-bot: note: canary with extra PT-asserts scheduled for tomorrow on canary pool.

anya: thanks — iterative plan: (1) repro harness + traces (oliver) (2) add PT-dup assert in dev builds (mira) (3) investigate async copy/fence ordering and free-list races (jason) (4) short-term pinning policy for affected customers.

oliver: will update BUG-3281 with repro and next steps once harness lands. cheers.
